decision: set a falsifiable report-v2 completion predicate
why: the graph can mis-rank evidence, so browser behavior and ordering must be measured
result: scope is one report boundary, three projections, bundled assets, docs, and browser proof

decision: captured the pre-change report and focused test baseline
why: the final proof needs measured old and new values
evidence: 72 focused tests; report 388297 bytes, 2 external scripts, 0 search controls, 0 confidence fields
result: baseline green; current report misses the target predicate

decision: Use AnalysisResult as the canonical envelope, add only confidence-enriched raw coupling evidence, and delete the Plotly/Cytoscape-specific transforms.
why: Prevents duplicated domain models and preserves numerator, denominators, raw ratio, and Wilson confidence in every view.

decision: Choose the investigation workspace prototype: master file grid, persistent selected-file evidence, and supplementary charts; graft the findings prototype's explicit non-causal language.
why: The workspace best supports repeated investigation; the dashboard is cramped and the findings view hides the complete corpus.

decision: Vendor ECharts 6.1.0 and Tabulator 6.5.2 with upstream licenses and SHA-256 manifest.
why: One chart runtime covers both spatial views; Tabulator earns its weight through virtualization, sorting, filtering, and keyboard controls. Generated reports make no CDN requests.

decision: Replace the monolithic CDN report with package assets, a 77-line Python facade, deterministic report data, and an investigation-workspace browser application.
why: Keeps the public API stable while reducing Python reader load and exposing ownership, defect, CI, X-Ray, and confidence evidence.
evidence: 335 tests passed; node syntax check; generated 110-file / 1008-pair report

decision: Prove offline composition, evidence ordering, escaping, full tests, all hooks, and wheel contents; do not retry unstable Chrome-for-Testing.
why: The in-app browser blocks file URLs and the user reported Chrome crashes, so interaction proof stops at deterministic document/JS contracts and the generated artifact is handed off for manual viewing.
evidence: 335 tests; all prek hooks; 1.79 MB wheel with assets; 2.44 MB generated report; 0 external script tags

decision: Narrow the offline claim to observable behavior and CSP enforcement; remove all remaining stale frozen-report documentation.
why: The bundled full Tabulator build contains unused remote-data APIs even though report code never invokes them; documentation must describe the enforced guarantee precisely.

decision: Keep Tabulator cells inline, open strongest evidence first, default to source and migrations, and make broader roles opt-in.
why: User screenshots showed vertically stacked cells, ascending zero-signal rows, and repository-support files overwhelming both file and coupling evidence.
evidence: 346 tests; all prek hooks; generated 125-file report reduced to 36 files and 130 code-to-code pairs in default scope

decision: Construct both Tabulator grids with their default scoped data, reserving asynchronous replacement for later scope changes.
why: Filling empty grids before Tabulator finished constructing created a startup race that could leave the report blank.
evidence: blank-startup regression contract; regenerated report contains constructor data; 346 tests

decision: Choose a grouped change landscape over a sunburst or ranked bars; add scope-relative heat meters to exact numeric table cells.
why: The grouped landscape preserves structural context without deep path whitespace; sunburst labels are ambiguous and bars duplicate the grid.
evidence: three-option visual sketch; 348 tests; all prek hooks; regenerated offline report

decision: Only file leaves render hotspot labels, while root and group nodes remain structural headings; use a taller canvas and compressed line-change area so small files remain legible.
why: ECharts supplies a synthetic root without file data, focus emphasis dimmed unrelated tiles, and raw line counts crushed smaller files into slivers.
evidence: failing regression contracts, then 350 tests and all hooks; regenerated 2.75 MB report with stable hierarchy and geometry

decision: Let workspace and chart cards fit their own content, inset the treemap by 12px, and replace repeated grid-link prose with accessible icon buttons.
why: Grid stretch made short tables and plots inherit a taller sibling's height, producing large blank regions; ECharts defaults also left unnecessary plot margins.
evidence: failing layout contracts, then 351 tests and all hooks; regenerated report uses compact independent card heights

decision: Use two independently flowing investigation columns and flatten them into deliberate file, evidence, scatter, landscape order on narrower screens.
why: Separate row grids still let the tall evidence panel hold both charts below it, leaving a column-sized void; default figure margins added hidden gutters.
evidence: failing page-structure contract, then 351 tests and all hooks; regenerated report has continuous desktop columns and explicit responsive order

decision: Increase the file viewport to a responsive 570px cap, place the dense landscape beneath it, and pair selected evidence with the shorter scatter plot; title the report literally.
why: The evidence rail remained taller than the file rail, so useful table capacity was traded for dead space; the original rhetorical heading obscured that the page presents evidence rather than a verdict.
evidence: failing composition and heading contracts, then 351 tests and all hooks; regenerated report balances the two rails and uses Repository evidence overview

decision: Add three scope-aware investigation leads that translate the strongest hotspot, supported coupling, and hotspot concentration into explicit next actions linked to their evidence.
why: A ranked table and charts still left the reader to infer what to do; high scores and coupling percentages are only useful when they change review and testing behaviour.
evidence: failing actionability contract, then 352 tests and all hooks; regenerated report opens with evidence-backed file, pair, and review-allocation actions
